items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: it was McCoy’s gig, McCoy Tyner, Joey Henderson, Henry Grimes and myself.

ctx.x: As time goes by I’ve spoken to musicians about searching for their own original sound or being creative, and I wonder if it gets harder as people come and go and they make their contributions and you’re trying to find something that hasn’t been done before. Does it get harder as the years go by?

Well not if you, you know assess the terrain, what’s going on. The most important thing is to find your own voice and just be real with that, and then go from there. And not be in competition, just being yourself. Having something that the music produces and fans can connect to. There’s one more album I’d like to say, it wasn’t my album but we have archive recordings here, and this is a recording from 1966 at the legendary club Slug’s and it’s McCoy Tyner, it was McCoy’s gig, McCoy Tyner, Joey Henderson, Henry…
